llm.summary: This skill matches its social-media lookup purpose, but it reads a local auth token, sends business queries to an external API, logs part of the token, and injects recurring payment links into responses.

dimensions.detail: Outbound requests are constrained to two allowlisted API endpoints, but user-supplied keywords, company names, domains, and AuthToken are sent to a third-party service without a clear privacy warning.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package install hooks, dependency scripts, or background setup were found; the manifest declares a URL installation record and Node as a required binary.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses strong mandatory instructions to append quota and upgrade/renewal footers to every result, including payment links, which goes beyond neutral result formatting.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill repeatedly reads a local skills-directory OraAgent.key credential file and logs the first eight token characters before each request; it does not install persistent services or write persistent state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The network API calls, keyword/domain searches, quota display, and AuthToken use are coherent with a paid social-media search service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only a token intended for this service, avoid submitting confidential lead lists or regulated customer data, and treat upgrade/renewal links in responses as provider-supplied commercial links. Operators should remove token-prefix logging, validate the payment URL, add a privacy notice, and escape or validate API-returned Markdown fields.
llm.findings:
[TP2] expected: Mixed Chinese and Latin text appears in the display name, but the functional skill id is ASCII and I found no visually spoofed tool name or hidden tool-redirection behavior.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill does use external network APIs and does not provide a manifest-level permission scope, although the executable code allowlists the two intended API URLs.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The local AuthToken file access is disclosed in the docs and purpose-aligned, but reading local credential material and transmitting business search terms externally is sensitive and under-disclosed to users.
[E1] expected: External transmission of search terms and AuthToken is core to the service, not hidden exfiltration, but it remains a user-facing confidentiality concern.
[SQP-3] expected: The English-translation behavior is presented as a data-source effectiveness constraint and allows explicit Chinese search, so I downgraded it to a product-behavior note rather than a security basis for the verdict.
[T01] unexpected: The mandatory payment/footer templates are artifact-backed and implemented in code; they are disclosed but overbearing enough to warrant Review.
[T09] unexpected: The token-prefix logging and unescaped Markdown rendering of remote API fields are artifact-backed implementation risks; they do not show malicious intent but increase phishing and data-exposure risk.
